1080	close to Shabbat, HaShem created the world
1081	through speech, and easily: "Let there be light," "Let us make man."
1082	The moment He said it, it came to be. Blessed is His name, and the world was. He
1083	doesn't need time. Surely HaShem did not do this
1084	because He was busy the whole time. So then,
1085	what is the proof? The Gemara in Sanhedrin speaks
1086	about the hours of Adam HaRishon: in the first hour he was created,
1087	in the second hour... and in the seventh hour, I think,
1088	he is already in the seventh hour, the eighth hour...
1089	in the seventh hour, I think, a soul was breathed into him. That is, in the seventh
1090	hour, HaShem actually finished
1091	His work.
1092	So this is many, many hours before the end
1093	of the day. So what happened? Did He afterward
1094	have to do more things? Was Adam HaRishon created last? No.
1095	Rather, there is something very deep here: that HaShem
1096	created these things on Erev Shabbat, bein hashmashot.
1097	There is a very deep meaning here. What is it?
1098	What is the meaning of Erev Shabbat bein hashmashot? Let's say
1099	it briefly.
1100	The world is built of body and soul. Everything created in the six
1101	days of creation is body. On Shabbat a soul enters the world.
1102	The soul was not created. The soul of the world
1103	is a supernal Divine light. This is really the Torah, for
1104	example. HaShem did not create
1105	the Torah in the six days of creation. Torah is the soul of
1106	the world. It preceded the world. Where? When was the Torah
1107	revealed? On Shabbat. All agree that on Shabbat the Torah was given.
1108	That is the soul. So Shabbat is not a creation. Shabbat is
1109	a transition.
1110	Good. So now, all I have is: in the act of creation HaShem created
1111	the body of the world, and on Shabbat He brought in the soul
1112	of the world. But at the seam between Shabbat and the six days
1113	of creation, what is called bein hashmashot? Bein hashmashot,
1114	according to the holy books, is called a connecting intermediary, because
1115	there are three times: weekday, Shabbat, and in the middle an intermediate point
1116	that connects. That is called bein hashmashot. There is a major inquiry
1117	about whether bein hashmashot is a doubt, since bein
1118	hashmashot is a doubt: perhaps day, perhaps night. So in the very depths,
1119	there is really no such thing as bein hashmashot, because
1120	it is either Friday or Shabbat, only you don't know. You
1121	treat it as a doubt. So the inquiry is whether bein
1122	hashmashot is really a time that does not exist
1123	and is only a doubt, so there is Friday until Shabbat,
1124	and from then it is Shabbat, or whether there really is such a time
1125	called bein hashmashot, which is called a connecting intermediary between
1126	Shabbat and the days of creation, which, so to speak, stands in the midst
1127	between them.
1128	What is the proof that it is a real intermediary,
1129	and not merely...? By the way, this is the opinion of the Ritva; there is a dispute
1130	among the Rishonim on this matter. The Ritva holds that bein hashmashot
1131	is an intermediary between them. A very deep topic. In any
1132	case, what is the proof? This is the proof: that HaShem
1133	created these things on Erev Shabbat, bein
1134	hashmashot. After all, there is no doubt before the Holy One, blessed be He.
1135	HaShem has no doubt; He knows exactly
1136	whether it is Friday or Shabbat. Only we have a doubt. "Who is
1137	in doubt?" There is no doubt with HaShem. So how
1138	can one say that HaShem created bein hashmashot?
1139	HaShem knows whether it is Friday or Shabbat. That
1140	is not called creating at bein hashmashot. Rather, from
1141	this we see proof that, simply, one could
1142	answer that in our time, we
1143	call it bein hashmashot, and HaShem created this,
1144	but for Him there was no doubt. But then it is not called bein hashmashot
1145	with regard to Him. On the contrary, if He created, it
1146	is a sign that it is Friday, right? Because one does not do work
1147	on Shabbat. So apparently... Rather, what is really true
1148	is that HaShem, specifically bein hashmashot, is an intermediate,
1149	connecting time. And what does that actually mean? That it is a time
1150	that comes to connect weekday and Shabbat.
1151	And there it is clear that the things that come to connect
1152	body and soul are neither from the body nor
1153	from the soul. They connect between them. What is this, for example?
1154	The writing. What is the writing? The writing is not the light itself,
1155	as we said before, but it is the way to reveal
1156	the light. The tablet too: in the end it is a tablet, but it is
1157	a way to reveal the encompassing light. That is, the hidden ideas
1158	of the Torah. For this HaShem created
1159	the letter, the writing. The Torah itself
1160	belongs to Shabbat; it is the light. But that which it
1161	is revealed and clothed in is the writing. It is found within.
1162	The same is true of the mouth of the earth, the mouth of the donkey, the staff of
1163	Elokim: all the things that perform miracles
1164	open nature to a passage toward the light. It is not the light
1165	itself, nor is it ordinary nature; it is a midpoint.
1166	They were created at bein hashmashot. So this writing,
1167	"the work of Elokim," and the Tablets, "the work of Elokim," are in fact
1168	at bein hashmashot. They come to express that there is here some special
1169	point of creation that came to allow the supernal light
1170	to be revealed through it. These are the letters of the Torah, together
1171	with the parchment,
1172	the tablet of the First Tablets, which is also "the work
1173	of Elokim," the supernal encompassing light. From this we
1174	learn the great merit of studying Torah with holiness,
1175	and of knowing that HaShem reveals Himself through the Torah.
1176	And this is the point of the taamei Torah, the hidden taam,
1177	the melody of the Torah, the song of the Torah, that we may merit,
1178	with the help of HaShem, to study Torah with joy, in holiness and purity.
1179	Amen. May it be His will.
